summary: Extended the newest finding from "a path is missing" to a three-stage, source-settled account, adding an error-attribution gap on the same layer. Stage one (unchanged): the repository's own compaction documentation states the duty ('the replicated log will grow large... two ways of compaction that can be initiated by users', with the example call on the instance, compaction.md:1-11) and the layer removes the path — spawn_actor consumes the instance (handle.rs:295), the handle has no accessor and no compaction method, the Command enum has no compaction request (event.rs:90-128), and the actor never calls op.trim()/op.snapshot(). Stage two (new): writing is fatal in the core — accept_entry_leader/accept_entries_leader call append_entry_with_batching(..).expect(WRITE_ERROR_MSG) (leader.rs:113-115, 124-127), the follower's flush and decision paths likewise (follower.rs:59, 100), the message being 'Error writing to storage.' (util.rs:357) — while the Storage trait defines a write error as an allowed, rolled-back outcome (storage/mod.rs:130-136). Stage three (new): that panic happens inside the task spawn_actor launches (handle.rs:295-323) with no join handle kept, and the layer's failure contract has no storage-error variant — the only value for an absent actor is AppendError::Shutdown / RuntimeProposeErr::Shutdown (handle.rs:164-165, 174-177, 237-240) — so an actor death caused by a target-internal fatal storage error reaches callers as the same value as an orderly shutdown, with the core's message lost. The four limits are recorded (source-only; the write-refusal premise not exercised; the panic itself is the core's documented design so the layer-side gap is the attribution; no source puts compaction out of scope). Standing findings unchanged: the event-backpressure park and cluster stall (8/64/1024, corrected transport, 21.69s bound), the core's missing accept-phase repair for a lost Accepted, and append_notify's false Ok for an unadopted index with the adopted-vs-unadopted boundary measured.
